title: Organic Chemistry I for Life Sciences
description: Structure, stereochemistry, substitution, elimination, and carbonyl chemistry taught through mechanism and reactivity rather than reaction memorization.

modifications: Clarified the typical E2 answer option as anti-periplanar; atypical syn elimination is not presented as equally typical.

outcomes.description: Draw valid resonance contributors and predict nucleophile/electrophile roles.
Use substrate, nucleophile, solvent, and leaving group to distinguish mechanisms.
Relate functional-group reactivity to biomolecular synthesis and degradation.

lesson_objectives.description: Use resonance without moving atoms or violating valence.
Predict how substrate structure and solvent affect substitution.
Connect mechanism to stereochemical outcome and rate law.
Predict alkene products while stating regioselectivity assumptions.
Explain why carbonyl carbon is electrophilic.
Predict addition versus substitution from the carbonyl derivative.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Structure, resonance, and acid-base reactivity
lessons.worked_example: A carboxylate conjugate base distributes negative charge over two oxygens, making a carboxylic acid more acidic than a typical alcohol whose alkoxide charge is localized.

lessons.title: Substitution mechanisms: SN1 and SN2
lessons.worked_example: A primary alkyl halide with a strong nucleophile in a polar aprotic solvent favors SN2; a tertiary substrate blocks backside attack and may favor ionization when a stable carbocation can form.

lessons.title: Elimination, alkenes, and stereochemical control
lessons.worked_example: In a cyclohexane chair, E2 requires a trans-diaxial beta hydrogen and leaving group; ring flip can expose the reactive conformation.

lessons.title: Carbonyl chemistry and acyl transfer
lessons.worked_example: An ester plus hydroxide forms a tetrahedral intermediate; collapse expels an alkoxide, followed by proton transfer to give a carboxylate under basic conditions.
